canonicalExplanation.summary: An event handler is a function you **pass** to React: `onClick={save}`. React calls it later, when the event happens. Writing `onClick={save()}` **calls** save immediately during render and passes its return value instead. When a handler needs arguments, wrap it: `onClick={() => remove(lesson.id)}`. Handlers are where you **compute state updates** and run **actions** like saving or navigating. Use real buttons and form submit so mouse, touch and keyboard all work; don't put onClick on a div.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A lesson editor's Save button sends a request every time the page renders, and clicking it does nothing. The code reads `<button onClick={save()}>Save</button>`. onClick={save} passes the function while onClick={save()} would execute during render. In this lesson you'll implement keyboard- and pointer-compatible interactions with correct handler arguments.

```predict
{"question": "`<button onClick={remove(lesson.id)}>Delete</button>` in a list of 5 lessons. What happens on first render?", "options": ["Nothing until clicked", "remove runs 5 times immediately, once per row"], "answer": 1, "why": "The parentheses call it during render. Write `onClick={() => remove(lesson.id)}`."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Props and composition** module, **Event propagation and delegation** (events and default actions), and **useState and snapshots**, since handlers usually set state.

examples.title: The save that ran on every render
examples.situation: onClick={save} passes the function while onClick={save()} would execute during render.
walkthrough: **Bug:** `onClick={save()}` ran save while rendering, so a request went out every render and the click did nothing.
**Pass the function:** `onClick={save}` hands React the function to call later.
**Check:** a test will render the editor, assert no save calls, then click Save and assert exactly one.
examples.result: No requests go out while rendering, and each click saves once.

examples.title: The delete buttons that fired together
examples.situation: A list renders `<button onClick={onDelete(l.id)}>` for each row, and opening the page deletes every lesson.
walkthrough: onDelete(l.id) ran during render for each row.
The fix needs a function that calls onDelete later with the id.
Write `onClick={() => onDelete(l.id)}` and give each button a name like "Delete Loops".
examples.result: Lessons are deleted only when their own button is pressed.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Event handler props should call the function immediately so React knows what to do later.
misconceptions.correction: React needs the function itself, to call when the event happens. Adding parentheses runs it during render. Pass the name, or an arrow that calls it with arguments.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The save that ran on every render", when did save run?

analogy.example: Passing a handler is like **giving someone your phone number** to call when the parcel arrives. Writing `save()` is like **calling them yourself right now**, before the parcel exists. An arrow with an argument is a note: "call this number and mention order 42".
limitations: Phones don't re-render; components do, and each render passes a fresh arrow.
A div with onClick is a doorbell with no button for some visitors.

steps.explanation: onClick={save} passes the function without running it.
Unlike onClick={save()}, nothing would execute during render.
React calls the handler when the learner clicks Save.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a correctly passed handler. Step 1, Render: onClick prop is function save; save calls is 0. onClick={save} passes the function without running it. nearTransfer.prompt: Add +1 and -1 buttons for a quantity, each calling `change(delta)`. Make sure Enter and Space work and nothing runs during render.

farTransfer.prompt: Build a small star rating that works with mouse, touch and keyboard (radio inputs or buttons). Test pointer clicks and keyboard selection, and check no handler runs during render.
expectedEvidence: Tests for both pointer and keyboard.

remediation.explanation: Look at every `on...={}`: **is there `()` right after a function name?** If yes, it runs during render. Pass the name, or wrap it in an arrow. And check the element is a real button, link or form control.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The delete buttons that fired together".

recap.summary: To implement keyboard- and pointer-compatible interactions, pass handler functions like onClick={save}, wrap calls needing arguments in arrows, compute state updates and actions inside handlers, and use native buttons and form submit so mouse, touch and keyboard all work.
